# M10 closed-form matting fixture

The fixture is generated by the pinned Python 3.12.11 interpreter with
PyMatting 1.1.15, NumPy 2.3.2, Pillow 12.2.0 and SciPy 1.17.0.  It executes
the checked `backgroundremover` wrapper at commit
`fa480627829759b902f8c233388d7aa67ab38099` and the installed PyMatting
functions; no model weights or network downloads are involved.

```sh
M10_PY=/path/to/pinned/python3.12
rm -rf /tmp/m10-authoritative /tmp/m10-reference /tmp/m10-smoke
NUMBA_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/m10-numba "$M10_PY" tests/fixtures/m10/run_authoritative_matting.py --output /tmp/m10-authoritative
"$M10_PY" tests/fixtures/m10/generate_m10_fixture.py --source /tmp/m10-authoritative --output /tmp/m10-reference
cp /tmp/m10-reference/authoritative-report.json tests/fixtures/m10/authoritative-report.json
cargo run -p bgremove-bench --offline --locked -- m10-smoke --output /tmp/m10-smoke
```

The first command executes the exact pinned PyMatting/backgroundremover source
chain and records all stage artifacts. The second assembles the checked parity
tree; copy its authoritative report when refreshing the tracked fixture. The
last command runs the Rust implementation and writes the deterministic smoke
artifacts. Use a Python 3.12.11 interpreter with the versions listed below;
the runner verifies every version and fails closed on drift.

The runner requires exactly Python 3.12.11, NumPy 2.3.2, Pillow 12.2.0,
SciPy 1.17.0 and PyMatting 1.1.15 and fails closed on source or runtime drift.
The smoke command computes the Rust artifacts and compares all captured stages
and the final RGBA image against `tests/fixtures/m10/reference/`. It invokes
the explicit `refine_backgroundremover_bounded` canonical-image/coarse-alpha
profile with `RembgTrimapConfig { foreground_threshold: 240,
background_threshold: 10, erode_size: 3 }` and `base_size=48`; the smoke
output includes canonical and working RGB/coarse/trimap/alpha/foreground and
background artifacts plus the connected final RGBA result. Generic callers
should use `refine_closed_form_with_coarse`; that API always honors the
caller-supplied trimap and uses class-preserving nearest-neighbour resizing
when bounded.
